questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm, and non-tender. Dark-field microscopy of the exudate shows motile spirochetes. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is caused by Treponema pallidum. First-line treatment is benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 28-year-old farmer presents with a slowly enlarging painless nodule on the dorsum of the hand that has been present for 3 months. It subsequently ulcerated and formed satellite lesions along the lymphatics up the arm. Gram stain is negative, but KOH mount shows cigar-shaped budding yeast. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: The sporotrichoid pattern (nodular lymphangitis), occupational exposure, and cigar-shaped budding yeast on KOH mount are diagnostic of Sporotrichosis caused by Sporothrix schenckii. Treatment is itraconazole 100-200 mg/day.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient with long-standing leprosy presents with sudden onset of painful erythematous nodules over the face, arms, and legs, fever, and neutrophilia. Biopsy shows granular finely dispersed bacilli and foam cells within the dermis without vasculitis. What is this reaction?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL / Type 2 reaction) occurs in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy. It is an immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity) reaction characterized by painful erythematous nodules, fever, and neutrophilia. Foam cells without vasculitis are characteristic. Treatment is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with a tense bullae on normal-appearing and erythematous skin, predominantly affecting the groin, axillae, and flexures. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the dermoepidermal junction. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae (negative Nikolsky sign), affects elderly predominantly, involves flexures, and DIF shows linear IgG+C3 at the BMZ. It targets BP180 and BP230 antigens in the hemidesmosome.

questions.q: A patient with SLE develops an erythematous photosensitive rash in a butterfly distribution over the malar area. ANA is positive at 1:320 with anti-dsDNA antibodies. Which complement pathway component is most classically consumed in active SLE leading to low serum levels?
questions.exp: Active SLE activates the classical complement pathway via immune complexes. Both C3 and C4 are consumed and their serum levels fall in active disease, making them useful markers of disease activity. C1q deficiency is associated with SLE predisposition.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a pearly, flesh-colored nodule with central ulceration and rolled, telangiectatic edges on the nose, present for 8 months. Histopathology shows basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on the nose (H-zone - high-risk area) is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, which offers the highest cure rate (>99%) with maximal tissue conservation. Peripheral palisading and retraction artifact are classic histological features.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with multiple oval scaly patches on the trunk following the lines of cleavage, preceded by a larger similar herald patch 2 weeks ago. The lesions show a 'fir tree' or 'Christmas tree' distribution. The most likely causative agent is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis rosea follows a 'Christmas tree' distribution along Langer's lines with a herald patch. It is associated with reactivation of HHV-6 and HHV-7. It is self-limiting. Oral erythromycin and acyclovir may shorten duration.

questions.q: A 40-year-old immunocompetent male with longstanding psoriasis is started on a new biologic therapy. After 3 months he develops a positive TB skin test and chest X-ray shows upper lobe infiltrates. Which biologic was most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Anti-TNF-α agents (adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab) significantly impair granuloma formation and are strongly associated with reactivation of latent TB. Screening for latent TB is mandatory before starting anti-TNF therapy. IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors carry lower TB reactivation risk.

questions.q: A 65-year-old male presents with an asymptomatic, velvety, hyperpigmented plaque on the posterior neck and axillae. He has a BMI of 38 and fasting blood glucose of 160 mg/dL. This skin sign is most characteristically associated with:
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans presents as velvety hyperpigmented plaques in body folds. It is most commonly associated with insulin resistance and obesity/Type 2 DM due to insulin stimulating keratinocyte proliferation via IGF-1 receptors. Malignant AN is associated with GI adenocarcinoma.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive male (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) presents with deeply pigmented, non-blanching, violaceous plaques on the lower extremities and palate. Biopsy shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and extravasated red blood cells. The causative virus is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by Human Herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8 / Kaposi's Sarcoma-associated Herpesvirus). It is an AIDS-defining malignancy. The classic histology includes spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and hemosiderin deposits. Treatment options include HAART, local therapy, or systemic chemotherapy (liposomal doxorubicin).

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with multiple grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the forehead and scalp with intense pain and hyperesthesia for 3 days. He now reports blurring of vision in the ipsilateral eye. The ocular complication most feared in this condition is:
opts: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with corneal dendritic ulcer
questions.exp: Herpes zoster affecting the nasociliary branch of V1 (Hutchinson's sign - vesicles on tip/side of nose) is associated with ocular involvement including keratitis with dendritic ulcers, episcleritis, and uveitis. Corneal dendritic ulcers are the most common serious ocular complication. Treatment: acyclovir 800mg 5x/day x7 days + ophthalmology referral.

questions.q: A 19-year-old female presents with pruritic wheals that appear and disappear within 24 hours without leaving any marks. She has had similar episodes daily for 8 weeks. Challenge tests are negative. The most appropriate first-line treatment is:
opts: Non-sedating H1 antihistamine (cetirizine/fexofenadine) at licensed dose
questions.exp: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) lasting >6 weeks with negative triggers is managed stepwise. Step 1 is a second-generation (non-sedating) H1 antihistamine at licensed doses. If inadequate at 2-4 weeks, updose up to 4x. Omalizumab is reserved for antihistamine-refractory CSU.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with hyperkeratotic, annular plaques with a hypopigmented center over the trunk. Skin smear shows AFB, and slit-skin smear bacteriological index (BI) is 3+. Nerve thickening is present. According to WHO classification, this patient has:
questions.exp: Multibacillary (MB) leprosy by WHO field criteria: >5 skin lesions OR positive slit-skin smear (any BI). This patient has a BI of 3+ which alone classifies as MB. MB MDT (rifampicin, clofazimine, dapsone) for 12 months is the treatment.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops skin thickening, Raynaud's phenomenon, and pitting scars on the fingertips. ANA is positive with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody. Which pattern of systemic sclerosis does she most likely have?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc), which has a worse prognosis with pulmonary fibrosis and renal crisis. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome).

questions.q: A 38-year-old male presents with recurrent purulent folliculitis in the beard area. Culture of pus grows Staphylococcus aureus sensitive to cloxacillin. The condition is clinically described as boggy swellings with multiple draining sinuses. The correct term for this severe form is:
questions.exp: Sycosis barbae (folliculitis barbae) is deep bacterial folliculitis of the beard area caused by S. aureus. The deep, boggy form with multiple follicular pustules and sinus tracts is called 'lupoid sycosis'. Treatment is systemic antibiotics (flucloxacillin/cloxacillin). Kerion is a fungal kerion (T. rubrum in beard = tinea barbae).

questions.q: A 7-year-old child presents with a painless, itchy, scaly plaque on the scalp with broken hairs at the follicular orifice. Wood's lamp examination shows bright green fluorescence. KOH mount shows hyphae within and around the hair shaft. This is:
questions.exp: Bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp and ectothrix pattern (hyphae outside the hair shaft) is characteristic of Microsporum canis. Endothrix infections (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum) do NOT fluoresce. Favus shows a dull yellow-green fluorescence.

questions.q: A 28-year-old sexually active woman presents with a profuse, frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge with intense pruritus. On examination, the cervix has a 'strawberry appearance'. Wet mount shows pear-shaped flagellated organisms. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Trichomoniasis is caused by Trichomonas vaginalis. Classical features include frothy yellow-green discharge, intense pruritus, strawberry cervix (colpitis macularis), and motile pear-shaped flagellated organisms on wet mount. Treatment: Metronidazole 2g single dose (treat partner simultaneously).

questions.q: During a Tzanck smear preparation from the base of a vesicle, the pathologist sees large multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear inclusions. This finding is seen in which conditions?
questions.exp: Tzanck smear positive (multinucleated giant cells / acantholytic cells) is seen in HSV-1, HSV-2, and VZV infections. Pemphigus also shows acantholytic cells but NOT multinucleated giant cells with inclusions. Molluscum shows Henderson-Patterson bodies.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male develops a rapidly enlarging, ulcerated nodule on the pinna of the ear over 2 months. Histopathology shows atypical squamous cells with keratin pearls invading beyond the dermis with perineural invasion. The most important prognostic factor distinguishing high-risk from low-risk SCC is:
opts: Tumor diameter >2 cm and depth >2 mm with poor differentiation
questions.exp: High-risk SCC features include: diameter >2 cm, depth >2 mm, poor differentiation, perineural/vascular invasion, immunosuppression, location on ear/lip, and recurrence. These features predict metastasis (5-10% in high risk vs <2% in low risk). Mohs surgery is recommended for high-risk SCC.

questions.q: A patient with severe generalized pustular psoriasis (von Zumbusch type) is hospitalized. Which of the following is the most appropriate systemic treatment in this acute setting?
questions.exp: Generalized pustular psoriasis (von Zumbusch) is a dermatological emergency with fever, leukocytosis, and sterile pustules. First-line systemic agents are acitretin (retinoid) or cyclosporine. IL-36 receptor antagonists (spesolimab/imsidolimab) are newer targeted options. Phototherapy and topical steroids are not appropriate acutely.

questions.q: A 35-year-old patient has multiple tender, erythematous nodules along the lower shins bilaterally. Biopsy from the leading edge (not the center) shows panniculitis predominantly affecting the septa without vasculitis. The most common cause of this condition is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum (EN) is a septal panniculitis without vasculitis. The most common cause globally is streptococcal pharyngitis (Group A Strep). Other causes: sarcoidosis, TB, IBD, drugs (OCP, sulfonamides), pregnancy, Yersinia. Biopsy from the leading edge avoids central necrosis artifacts.

questions.q: A dermatologist uses dermoscopy to evaluate a pigmented lesion. Which dermoscopic feature is most specific for melanoma?
questions.exp: Blue-white veil (irregular, structureless area of confluent blue-grey pigmentation with a white ground-glass haze) is a specific dermoscopic feature of melanoma, corresponding to acanthotic epidermis over compact orthokeratosis above melanin-containing cells. Comma vessels suggest dermal nevus; strawberry pattern suggests sebaceous hyperplasia; moth-eaten border suggests seborrheic keratosis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on long-term hydroxychloroquine develops a bull's eye maculopathy on ophthalmological screening. With respect to the skin, hydroxychloroquine is used in which condition?
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine (an antimalarial) is a cornerstone treatment for discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE), subacute cutaneous lupus, and systemic LE. Retinal toxicity (bull's eye maculopathy) is a dose-dependent adverse effect requiring annual ophthalmological screening. Maximum safe dose is 5 mg/kg/day.

questions.q: A 6-month-old infant presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the mouth and nose that began as vesicles. Gram stain of the crust shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. The treatment of choice for non-bullous impetigo affecting a small area is:
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo caused by S. aureus (or GAS) in limited areas is treated with topical mupirocin 2% ointment (or fusidic acid) applied TID for 5-7 days. Retapamulin is another option. Systemic antibiotics (cefalexin/cloxacillin) are used for extensive disease or when topical therapy fails.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with 15-year history of recurrent blistering after minimal trauma on the dorsa of the hands and forearms. Milia and scars are present. Urine turns dark reddish-brown on exposure to sunlight. Which enzyme is deficient in this condition?
questions.exp: Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) presents with photomechanical fragility, blisters, milia, and hypertrichosis on sun-exposed areas. It is caused by deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase. Urine shows pink-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp and elevated uroporphyrins. Treatment: phlebotomy or low-dose hydroxychloroquine.

questions.q: A 24-year-old male presents with multiple condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts). Which HPV serotypes are responsible for the majority of anogenital warts?
questions.exp: HPV 6 and 11 are low-risk types responsible for >90% of anogenital warts (condyloma acuminata). HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic types causing cervical, anal, and penile carcinoma. HPV 1 and 2 cause plantar and common warts. Treatment options: podophyllotoxin, imiquimod, cryotherapy, or trichloroacetic acid.

questions.q: A 33-year-old male with no prior skin history develops a widespread erythematous morbilliform rash 10 days after starting amoxicillin-clavulanate for a dental abscess. He is also found to have lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytosis, and elevated liver enzymes. The most likely diagnosis is:
opts: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)
questions.exp: DRESS (Drug Hypersensitivity Syndrome) classically presents 2-8 weeks after drug initiation with morbilliform rash, facial edema, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytosis, eosinophilia, and multi-organ involvement (liver, kidney, lung). Common culprit drugs: aromatic anticonvulsants (carbamazepine, phenytoin), allopurinol, dapsone, minocycline. Mortality 10%.

questions.q: During a punch biopsy of a bullous lesion on the forearm, the dermatologist should ideally sample from which area for best histopathological yield?
opts: The center of an old ruptured bulla
The edge of an early intact bulla (including perilesional skin)
The base of a recently deroofed bulla
questions.exp: For bullous disorders, the ideal biopsy is from the edge of an early, intact blister including perilesional skin. This preserves the roof-to-floor architecture needed to determine the level of cleavage (intraepidermal vs. subepidermal). Old or ruptured bullae show secondary changes making diagnosis difficult. DIF is performed on perilesional normal skin (4mm punch in separate specimen).

questions.q: A 29-year-old with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes mellitus develops painful, rapidly spreading necrosis of the scrotum with crepitus on palpation. Imaging shows gas in the soft tissues. The most appropriate initial management is:
opts: Emergency surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
Topical antiseptic dressings and oral antibiotics
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a necrotizing fasciitis of the genitoperineal region, often polymicrobial (anaerobes + gram negatives). It is a surgical emergency requiring immediate wide surgical debridement as the cornerstone of management, combined with broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (covering anaerobes, gram-positives, gram-negatives). Delay in surgery significantly increases mortality.

questions.q: A 45-year-old presents with diffuse hair loss showing a bimodal peak on hair pull test, predominantly telogen hairs. The patient had a severe febrile illness 3 months ago. The most likely diagnosis and expected prognosis is:
opts: Acute telogen effluvium - usually self-limiting with full regrowth
questions.exp: Telogen effluvium (TE) follows a trigger (fever, surgery, severe illness, postpartum, crash dieting) by 2-3 months when anagen follicles prematurely enter telogen and shed. Hair pull test shows predominantly telogen hairs (club hairs). TE is usually self-limiting with complete regrowth in 6-12 months once the trigger resolves.

questions.q: A 62-year-old presents with a thick, warty, verrucous plaque on the dorsum of the foot, present for 12 years. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, rounded sclerotic bodies (Medlar bodies/copper penny bodies) with septation. The causative organisms are:
opts: Fonsecaea pedrosoi and Cladophialophora carrionii (dematiaceous fungi)
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic fungal infection caused by dematiaceous (melanized/brown-black) fungi, most commonly Fonsecaea pedrosoi. Characteristic histology shows Medlar bodies (sclerotic bodies / copper penny bodies) - brown, rounded, thick-walled cells with transverse septation. Treatment: itraconazole or terbinafine long-term, combined with local heat therapy.
